blocks.note: For general counting, よん・なな・きゅう are useful defaults. Other readings depend on the counter; see the alternatives below.
Build the teens with 十 + the single digit. Twenty is 二 + 十.
Single digit + 十. Forty is よんじゅう, seventy ななじゅう, ninety きゅうじゅう.

blocks.heading: Hundreds
blocks.note: Orange marks sound changes: 300 さんびゃく, 600 ろっぴゃく, 800 はっぴゃく. Say 百 for 100, not 一百.

blocks.heading: Thousands
blocks.note: Orange marks 3,000 さんぜん and 8,000 はっせん. Say 千 for 1,000; 一千 is also used in some contexts.

blocks.heading: Ten-thousands & larger
blocks.note: Japanese groups large numbers by 10,000: 万 = 10,000 and 億 = 100,000,000. Unlike 百 and 千, 10,000 normally includes 一: 一万.

blocks.heading: Putting numbers together

numberRows.reading: さんびゃくろくじゅうご
numberRows.speech: さんびゃくろくじゅうご

numberRows.reading: せんにひゃくさんじゅうよん
numberRows.speech: せんにひゃくさんじゅうよん

numberRows.reading: いちまんにせんさんびゃくよんじゅうご
numberRows.speech: いちまんにせんさんびゃくよんじゅうご

blocks.note: Read from the largest unit to the smallest. Do not read a zero for an empty place: 101 is ひゃくいち.

blocks.heading: Alternative readings
blocks.note: These are context-dependent alternatives, not replacements everywhere. Examples: 四月 しがつ, 七時 しちじ, 九月 くがつ. Later pages cover these counter-specific readings.

blocks.japanese: 百一(ひゃくいち)
blocks.speech: ひゃくいち

blocks.japanese: 全部(ぜんぶ)で二十(にじゅう)です。
blocks.speech: ぜんぶでにじゅうです。

blocks.japanese: 番号(ばんごう)は四十二(よんじゅうに)です。
blocks.speech: ばんごうわよんじゅうにです。

blocks.heading: 1st–10th · memorize these
blocks.note: The 1st is ついたち (calendar date), not いちにち (one day). Distinguish 4日 よっか from 8日 ようか; 6日 is むいか and 9日 is ここのか.

blocks.heading: 11th–20th
blocks.note: Key exceptions: 14日 じゅうよっか, 17日 じゅうしちにち, 19日 じゅうくにち, 20日 はつか. Orange marks readings to pay particular attention to.

blocks.heading: 21st–31st
blocks.note: 24日 is にじゅうよっか; 27日 にじゅうしちにち; 29日 にじゅうくにち. Some speakers use なな for 17/27; this page uses the しち readings in the Japan Foundation date chart.

blocks.heading: Ask the date
blocks.note: 何日 is read なんにち. Dates and durations can share forms: 三日 can mean the 3rd or three days; 三日間 clearly means a three-day period. Duration will have its own page.

blocks.japanese: 今日(きょう)は何日(なんにち)ですか。
誕生日(たんじょうび)は四月八日(しがつようか)です。
予約(よやく)は十四日(じゅうよっか)です。
二十日(はつか)に会(あ)いましょう。
次(つぎ)の休(やす)みは二十四日(にじゅうよっか)です。
blocks.english: My next day off is the 24th.

blocks.heading: January–December
blocks.note: Month names use がつ. Remember April しがつ, July しちがつ, September くがつ. A duration in months uses かげつ; that comes on a separate page.

blocks.heading: Calendar years

numberRows.reading: にせんにじゅうよねん
numberRows.speech: にせんにじゅうよねん

numberRows.reading: にせんにじゅうろくねん
numberRows.speech: にせんにじゅうろくねん

numberRows.reading: にせんにじゅうしちねん
numberRows.speech: にせんにじゅうしちねん

numberRows.reading: にせんにじゅうきゅうねん
numberRows.speech: にせんにじゅうきゅうねん

blocks.note: Read the whole number, then 年（ねん）. A year ending in 4 uses よねん, not よんねん. This page uses しちねん for 7; ななねん is also common. 9年 is きゅうねん.

blocks.heading: Relative months & years
blocks.note: 毎月 can also be read まいげつ, and 毎年 まいねん. This page uses the common conversational readings まいつき and まいとし.

blocks.japanese: 今(いま)は何月(なんがつ)ですか。
誕生日(たんじょうび)は七月(しちがつ)です。
来月(らいげつ)、日本(にほん)に行(い)きます。
blocks.english: I’m going to Japan next month.

blocks.japanese: この包丁(ほうちょう)は二千二十四年(にせんにじゅうよねん)に買(か)いました。
予約(よやく)は十月七日(じゅうがつなのか)です。

blocks.heading: Monday–Sunday
blocks.note: All seven names end in ようび. Keep よう as a long vowel. Calendars often abbreviate them as 月・火・水・木・金・土・日.

blocks.heading: Relative days
blocks.note: This page uses conversational readings: おととい, きのう, きょう, あした, あさって. Preserve the long vowels in きのう and きょう, and the doubled consonant in あさって.

blocks.heading: Useful day words
blocks.note: 何曜日 asks the day of the week; 何日 asks the calendar date. 平日 usually means Monday–Friday excluding public holidays.

blocks.japanese: 今日(きょう)は何曜日(なんようび)ですか。
blocks.english: What day of the week is it today?

blocks.japanese: 月曜日(げつようび)は休(やす)みです。
金曜日(きんようび)に会(あ)おう。
明日(あした)、市場(いちば)に行(い)きます。
blocks.english: I’m going to the market tomorrow.

blocks.japanese: 週末(しゅうまつ)は何(なに)する？
blocks.english: What are you doing this weekend?

blocks.heading: Hours: 1–12
blocks.note: Clock hours use じ: 4時 よじ, 7時 しちじ, 9時 くじ. 7時 can also be ななじ. A duration in hours uses じかん; that comes on a separate page.

blocks.heading: Minutes: 1–10
blocks.note: Listen for ふん → ぷん and doubled consonants. 4分 can also be よんふん, 8分 はちふん, and 10分 じっぷん. This page uses よんぷん・はっぷん・じゅっぷん.

blocks.heading: Useful minute marks
blocks.note: Build other minutes from tens + the final digit: 21分 にじゅういっぷん. Half past can be said as ～時半.

blocks.heading: AM, PM & questions
blocks.note: Read times as hour + minute: 7:15 しちじじゅうごふん. 午前 is before noon; 午後 is after noon. In 24-hour notation, 14:00 is じゅうよじ; 0:00 is れいじ.

numberRows.reading: ごごにじよんじゅうごふん
numberRows.speech: ごごにじよんじゅうごふん

blocks.japanese: 今(いま)、何時(なんじ)ですか。
朝(あさ)は七時半(しちじはん)に起(お)きます。
blocks.english: I get up at 7:30 in the morning.

blocks.japanese: 予約(よやく)は午後六時(ごごろくじ)です。
九時十五分(くじじゅうごふん)に会(あ)おう。
お店(みせ)は十時(じゅうじ)からです。

blocks.heading: Hours: 1–10
blocks.note: Hours of duration use じかん, not clock-time じ. This page uses しちじかん and くじかん; ななじかん and きゅうじかん are also used.

blocks.heading: Days: 1–10
blocks.note: One day is いちにち; the 1st of the month is ついたち. From two days onward, the forms match the calendar dates. Add 間（かん）to emphasize a period: 三日間 みっかかん.

blocks.heading: Weeks: 1–10
blocks.note: Watch the doubled consonants in 1・8・10 weeks. 10週間 can also be じっしゅうかん.

blocks.heading: Months: 1–10
blocks.note: Duration uses かげつ: 一か月 いっかげつ. January is 一月 いちがつ. 8か月 can also be はちかげつ; 10か月 じっかげつ.

blocks.heading: Years: 1–10
blocks.note: 4年 is よねん. This page uses しちねん for 7年; ななねん is also common. Add 間（かん）when helpful: 一年間 いちねんかん.

blocks.heading: Half & questions
blocks.note: Minutes work the same way for a duration as for clock time; see the previous page. どのくらい asks “how long?” more generally.

blocks.japanese: 駅(えき)まで一時間(いちじかん)ぐらいかかります。
blocks.english: It takes about an hour to get to the station.

blocks.japanese: 日本(にほん)に三日間(みっかかん)滞在(たいざい)します。
blocks.english: I’ll stay in Japan for three days.

blocks.japanese: 一週間(いっしゅうかん)、休(やす)みを取(と)ります。
日本語(にほんご)を六(ろっ)か月(げつ)勉強(べんきょう)しています。
blocks.english: I’ve been studying Japanese for six months.
blocks.speech: にほんごをろっかげつべんきょうしています。

blocks.japanese: この包丁(ほうちょう)は四年(よねん)使(つか)っています。
blocks.english: I’ve been using this knife for four years.

blocks.heading: People: 1–10
blocks.note: Use 人 for people. Memorize 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり, 四人 よにん. This page uses ななにん for 7; しちにん is also used.

blocks.heading: Larger groups & questions
blocks.note: Above ten, use the number + にん: 11人 じゅういちにん, 12人 じゅうににん. A final 4 uses よにん: 14人 じゅうよにん. 何人 asks how many people.

blocks.heading: Together or on your own
blocks.note: ～人で describes the group doing something together. 一人で means alone / on your own. For restaurant reservations, you may also hear the polite counter 名（めい）.

blocks.japanese: 何人(なんにん)ですか。
二人(ふたり)です。
四人(よにん)で予約(よやく)したいです。
blocks.english: I’d like to make a reservation for four.

blocks.japanese: 今日(きょう)は一人(ひとり)で食(た)べます。
blocks.english: I’m eating on my own today.

blocks.japanese: 三人(さんにん)で行(い)こう。
blocks.english: Let’s go, the three of us.

blocks.heading: General things: 〜つ
blocks.note: A useful general counter for things and orders. Memorize these forms; ten is とお, without つ. This set stops at ten. Use a suitable counter such as 個 for larger numbers. Use 人 for people.

blocks.heading: Small individual objects: 〜個
blocks.note: 個 counts individual objects such as eggs, apples and small items. Watch いっこ・ろっこ・はっこ・じゅっこ. 10個 can also be じっこ.

blocks.heading: Questions & larger numbers
blocks.note: いくつ is the general “how many?” question; 何個 asks specifically for individual objects. Put the count after the object and particle: 卵を二個買います.

blocks.japanese: これを一(ひと)つください。
blocks.speech: これをひとつください。

blocks.japanese: 卵(たまご)を二個(にこ)買(か)います。
blocks.speech: たまごをにこかいます。

blocks.japanese: おにぎりを三(みっ)つお願(ねが)いします。
blocks.speech: おにぎりをみっつおねがいします。

blocks.japanese: りんごは何個(なんこ)ありますか。
blocks.speech: りんごはなんこありますか。

blocks.japanese: あといくつ必要(ひつよう)？
blocks.english: How many more do we need?
blocks.speech: あといくつひつよう？

blocks.heading: Long objects: 〜本
blocks.note: 本 counts long, narrow objects such as bottles, pencils, bananas and cucumbers. Listen for ほん → ぽん / ぼん. 10本 can also be じっぽん. Books use 冊, even though the word for a book is 本（ほん）.

blocks.heading: Cups & glasses: 〜杯
blocks.note: 杯 counts drinks served in cups or glasses, and bowlfuls such as rice. Listen for はい → ぱい / ばい. 10杯 can also be じっぱい. A bottle of water uses 本; a glass of water uses 杯.

blocks.heading: Ask how many
blocks.note: The question words use the voiced forms ぼん and ばい. 一杯 means one cup here; いっぱい can also mean “a lot” in other contexts.

blocks.japanese: きゅうりを三本(さんぼん)買(か)います。
blocks.speech: きゅうりをさんぼんかいます。

blocks.japanese: 水(みず)を二本(にほん)ください。
blocks.speech: みずをにほんください。

blocks.japanese: ビールを一杯(いっぱい)お願(ねが)いします。
blocks.speech: びーるをいっぱいおねがいします。

blocks.japanese: コーヒーは何杯(なんばい)飲(の)んだ？
blocks.english: How many cups of coffee did you drink?
blocks.speech: こーひーはなんばいのんだ？

blocks.japanese: もう一杯(いっぱい)どう？
blocks.speech: もういっぱいどう？

entries.kanji: 枚(まい)・冊(さつ)・台(だい)

blocks.heading: Flat items: 〜枚
blocks.note: 枚 counts thin, flat things such as sheets of paper, plates, tickets and shirts. No consonant changes: いちまい・ろくまい・はちまい.

blocks.heading: Books & notebooks: 〜冊
blocks.note: 冊 counts bound items such as books, notebooks and magazines. Watch いっさつ・はっさつ・じゅっさつ. 10冊 can also be じっさつ. A book is 本（ほん）, but its counter is 冊.

blocks.heading: Machines & vehicles: 〜台
blocks.note: 台 counts machines, appliances and vehicles such as cars, bicycles, computers and refrigerators. No consonant changes: いちだい・ろくだい・はちだい.

blocks.japanese: お皿(さら)を四枚(よんまい)用意(ようい)します。
blocks.speech: おさらをよんまいよういします。

blocks.japanese: 紙(かみ)を一枚(いちまい)ください。
blocks.speech: かみをいちまいください。

blocks.japanese: 料理(りょうり)の本(ほん)を二冊(にさつ)買(か)いました。
blocks.speech: りょうりのほんをにさつかいました。

blocks.japanese: ノートは何冊(なんさつ)必要(ひつよう)？
blocks.english: How many notebooks do we need?
blocks.speech: のーとはなんさつひつよう？

blocks.japanese: 家(いえ)に自転車(じてんしゃ)が二台(にだい)あります。
blocks.english: We have two bicycles at home.
blocks.speech: いえにじてんしゃがにだいあります。

blocks.heading: Age: 1–10
blocks.note: 歳 counts years of age. Watch いっさい・はっさい・じゅっさい. 4歳 is よんさい, unlike 4年 よねん. 10歳 can also be じっさい.

blocks.heading: Teens & twenties
blocks.note: 20歳 has the special reading はたち; にじゅっさい is also correct. Other ages combine tens + the final digit: 21歳  にじゅういっさい.

blocks.heading: Tens & questions
blocks.note: 何歳ですか asks age. おいくつですか is a more polite wording. In casual conversation, 何歳？ is common.

blocks.japanese: 何歳(なんさい)ですか。
blocks.speech: なんさいですか。

blocks.japanese: 妹(いもうと)は二十歳(はたち)です。
blocks.speech: いもうとははたちです。

blocks.japanese: 来月(らいげつ)、三十歳(さんじゅっさい)になります。
blocks.speech: らいげつ、さんじゅっさいになります。

blocks.japanese: 子供(こども)は八歳(はっさい)です。
blocks.speech: こどもははっさいです。

blocks.japanese: 弟(おとうと)は今(いま)、何歳(なんさい)？
blocks.english: How old is your younger brother now?
blocks.speech: おとうとはいま、なんさい？

entries.kanji: 回数(かいすう)・順番(じゅんばん)

blocks.heading: Number of times: 〜回
blocks.note: 回 counts how many times an action happens. Watch いっかい・ろっかい・はっかい・じゅっかい. 10回 can also be じっかい. Frequency: 一週間に二回 = twice a week.

blocks.heading: Numbers & positions: 〜番
blocks.note: 番 identifies numbers or positions, such as numbered tickets. Add 目（め）for a position in a sequence: 二番目 = second. 回目 counts an occurrence: 二回目 = the second time.

blocks.japanese: 一週間(いっしゅうかん)に二回(にかい)、日本語(にほんご)を勉強(べんきょう)します。
blocks.english: I study Japanese twice a week.
blocks.speech: いっしゅうかんににかい、にほんごをべんきょうします。

blocks.japanese: もう一回(いっかい)言(い)ってください。
blocks.english: Please say it one more time.
blocks.speech: もういっかいいってください。

blocks.japanese: 日本(にほん)に何回(なんかい)行(い)った？
blocks.english: How many times have you been to Japan?
blocks.speech: にほんになんかいいった？

blocks.japanese: 番号(ばんごう)は三番(さんばん)です。
blocks.speech: ばんごうはさんばんです。

blocks.japanese: 今回(こんかい)は二回目(にかいめ)です。
blocks.speech: こんかいはにかいめです。

blocks.heading: Yen: 1–10
blocks.note: Read 円 as えん, joined to the number. 4円 is よえん; 7円 ななえん; 9円 きゅうえん.

blocks.heading: Common price building blocks
blocks.note: Keep the number sound changes from page 1, then add えん. Japanese large numbers group around 万（10,000）: 一万円 is 10,000 yen.

blocks.heading: Putting prices together

numberRows.reading: よんひゃくはちじゅうえん
numberRows.speech: よんひゃくはちじゅうえん

numberRows.reading: せんにひゃくはちじゅうえん
numberRows.speech: せんにひゃくはちじゅうえん

blocks.note: Read the amount as one connected number, followed by 円. 400円 is よんひゃくえん even though 4円 is よえん.

blocks.japanese: これはいくらですか。
blocks.speech: これはいくらですか。

blocks.japanese: この包丁(ほうちょう)は一万二千円(いちまんにせんえん)です。
blocks.speech: このほうちょうはいちまんにせんえんです。

blocks.japanese: 全部(ぜんぶ)で二千五百円(にせんごひゃくえん)です。
blocks.speech: ぜんぶでにせんごひゃくえんです。

blocks.japanese: 千円(せんえん)でお願(ねが)いします。
blocks.speech: せんえんでおねがいします。

blocks.japanese: お釣(つ)りは五百円(ごひゃくえん)です。
blocks.speech: おつりはごひゃくえんです。

blocks.heading: Animals: 〜匹
blocks.note: 匹 counts small animals such as cats, dogs, fish and insects. Watch ひき → ぴき / びき: いっぴき・さんびき・ろっぴき・はっぴき・じゅっぴき. 10匹 can also be じっぴき. Birds usually use 羽; large animals such as horses use 頭.

blocks.heading: Building floors: 〜階
blocks.note: 階 counts building floors. This page uses さんがい for 3階; さんかい is also correct. 8階 can also be はちかい; 10階 じっかい. In Japan, 1階 is the ground floor. 回 counts occurrences; 階 counts floors, even when their readings sound alike.

blocks.heading: Questions & basement
blocks.note: Question forms: 何匹 なんびき, 何階 なんがい. 地下（ちか）means below ground; 地下一階 is B1.

blocks.japanese: 猫(ねこ)を二匹(にひき)飼(か)っています。
blocks.speech: ねこをにひきかっています。

blocks.japanese: 魚(さかな)が三匹(さんびき)います。
blocks.speech: さかながさんびきいます。

blocks.japanese: レストランは三階(さんがい)にあります。
blocks.english: The restaurant is on the third floor.
blocks.speech: れすとらんはさんがいにあります。

blocks.japanese: お店(みせ)は何階(なんがい)ですか。
blocks.english: Which floor is the shop on?
blocks.speech: おみせはなんがいですか。

blocks.japanese: 地下一階(ちかいっかい)に行(い)こう。
blocks.english: Let’s go to basement level one.
blocks.speech: ちかいっかいにいこう。

entries.kanji: 料理(りょうり)で数(かぞ)える

blocks.heading: Servings: 〜人前
blocks.note: 人前 counts portions intended for people. 一人前 is いちにんまえ, and 二人前 ににんまえ; these differ from 一人 ひとり and 二人 ふたり.

blocks.heading: Platefuls / dishes served: 〜皿
blocks.note: 皿 counts food served on plates. Empty plates usually use 枚: 皿を二枚. Two plated dishes: 二皿 ふたさら.

blocks.heading: Slices / cut pieces: 〜切れ
blocks.note: 切れ counts cut pieces such as fish fillets, slices of bread or pieces of cake. This page uses the native readings ひときれ・ふたきれ・みきれ.

blocks.heading: Tablespoons & teaspoons
blocks.note: Japanese measuring spoons: 大さじ = 15 mL, 小さじ = 5 mL. Recipes often write 大さじ1 / 小さじ1. With 杯 explicitly: 大さじ一杯 おおさじいっぱい.

blocks.heading: Rice & cups
blocks.note: A standard Japanese recipe cup is 200 mL. The rice-measuring cup for 1合 is 180 mL; these are different cups.

blocks.heading: Small amounts
blocks.note: ひとつまみ is a pinch, commonly taken with three fingertips. 少々 is a small amount, commonly taken with two fingertips for salt; the exact amount depends on the ingredient.

blocks.japanese: 二人前(ににんまえ)お願(ねが)いします。
blocks.speech: ににんまえおねがいします。

blocks.japanese: 刺身(さしみ)を一皿(ひとさら)ください。
blocks.speech: さしみをひとさらください。

blocks.japanese: 鮭(さけ)を二切れ(ふたきれ)焼(や)きます。
blocks.english: I’ll grill two pieces of salmon.
blocks.speech: さけをふたきれやきます。

blocks.japanese: 醤油(しょうゆ)を大(おお)さじ二(に)入(い)れます。
blocks.english: Add two tablespoons of soy sauce.
blocks.speech: しょうゆをおおさじにいれます。

blocks.japanese: 砂糖(さとう)を小(こ)さじ一(いち)入(い)れます。
blocks.speech: さとうをこさじいちいれます。

blocks.japanese: 米(こめ)を二合(にごう)炊(た)きます。
blocks.english: I’ll cook two gō of rice.
blocks.speech: こめをにごうたきます。

blocks.japanese: 塩(しお)をひとつまみ加(くわ)えます。
blocks.speech: しおをひとつまみくわえます。
